events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.12 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
RydeTAXI trip Clarke Quay → Sentosa Beach Station; the fare is metered, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly (F6) [RD-2]. The GPS record shows the actual distance 10.9 km against an optimal 7.9 km (+3.0 km) [F1], and identifies one off-route segment 18:32–18:39 that drove 3.32 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment is a deviation and must be reviewed for exemption; no threshold applies, and the fare differential is billed as $4.21 = 3.0 km × $1.41/km [F4][RD-1].

Exemption under RD-5 fails. The driver's chat message asks "Traffic ahead on Kampong Bahru Road is building up, ok if I go round via Outram Road?" at 18:28 [F7], but there is no rider reply in the record; the driver's own statement concedes only that there was "no objection" [F8]. Silence is not the explicit agreement RD-5 requires, and RD-5 expressly excludes the case where the driver changed route and informed the rider afterwards or the rider did not reply [F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply either: this is a driver-proposed route, not a rider-named stop, so the segment cannot be exempted on that basis [F3][RD-3].

Exemption under RD-4 also fails. The traffic facts show only speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway [F9][F10] — band 3 is not band 1 or 2, and a band record alone does not exempt a segment in any event [RD-4(b)]. No LTA traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch, reported before the detour, exists in the record [F11], and weather was fair with no rain [F12]; so RD-4(a) is not satisfied [RD-4]. The segment is therefore a non-exempt detour and triggers RD-2.

Amount (RydeTAXI, RD-2): only the excess kilometres of the non-exempt segment are refunded, at the trip's per-km rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.4064/km [F3][F6][RD-2]. Awarded at the tariff-consistent rate of $1.41/km: 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.1161 ≈ $3.12 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Waiting was $0.00 and no ERP is claimed, so nothing further is refundable [F6][FARE-2]. The residual difference between the $4.21 billed excess and the segment sum is map-matching residual and is not refunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no account flag [F14][RD-6].

Both briefs request no_action. That is rejected: the GPS segment record [F3] plus the absence of any pre-agreed route change [F7][F8] establishes an unexplained deviation under RD-1 and a refundable amount under RD-2. The rider's own account history (0 upheld disputes) [F13] is profile material only and does not decide the case [RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.12 (voucher, NS-7) to the rider for the non-exempt detour segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's account; no account flag (RD-6 not met).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip. The GPS record shows the driver took a longer route than needed, adding about 2.2 km of non-exempt detour. The driver messaged about a possible route change, but there was no reply from you, so it wasn't agreed in advance. We're refunding S$3.12 for that portion. It's paid as a Ryde voucher, which you'll receive shortly. Nothing else on the fare was refundable. Your account stays in good standing.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip. The GPS record shows a detour of about 2.2 km where your message proposing a different route got no reply from the rider, so it wasn't agreed in advance. The traffic conditions on record didn't meet the exemption criteria either. Outcome: S$3.12 refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and a route deviation breach recorded on your account. No account flag was applied. Please confirm route changes with the rider before deviating.
